description: The Gemini Near-InfraRed Spectrograph (GNIRS) is a versatile 1.0 to 5.4 micron instrument mounted on Gemini North providing long-slit, cross-dispersed, and integral-field spectroscopy as well as acquisition imaging. Its filter wheels hold broad-band near-infrared filters and narrow-band order-sorting and emission-line filters.
facility_description: The International Gemini Observatory operates twin 8.1-meter optical and infrared telescopes atop Maunakea in Hawai'i (Gemini North) and Cerro Pachón in Chile (Gemini South), managed by NSF NOIRLab.
notes: GNIRS filter transmissions include Mauna Kea near-infrared broad-band filters (J_MK, K_MK), broad-band blue/red cut filters, and narrow-band filters (H2, PAH). Laboratory transmission scans are distributed on Gemini instrumentation pages; redistribution terms are not specified under NOIRLab open content policy.
